plants.name: Jacaranda mimosifolia
plants.description: Bare, graceful branches disappear under clouds of trumpet-shaped, lavender-blue blossoms. Streets and parks across the city turn violet, and the fallen flowers carpet the pavement beneath the trees.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late October through November, with peak bloom in early November across much of Australia
plants.location: Eastern Australia, including Brisbane and Sydney's streets and parks
plants.funFact: Jacarandas are native to South America, not Australia. They flower on nearly leafless branches, which is why a whole avenue reads as one solid block of colour.

plants.name: Camellia sasanqua
plants.description: This is the early act of the camellia world. Glossy evergreen shrubs open delicate, often lightly scented single or semi-double blooms with golden stamens, brightening the cooler days of autumn.
plants.bloomingSeason: Autumn into early winter, commonly starting in October or November and continuing through December or January
plants.location: Temperate gardens of Japan, the southeastern United States and other mild-climate regions of the Northern Hemisphere
plants.funFact: Camellia sasanqua is a close relative of the tea plant. Its seeds are pressed for camellia oil, a traditional hair and skin treatment in Japan.

plants.name: Chrysanthemum × morifolium
plants.description: Dense, many-petalled blooms in rich autumn shades fill Japan's gardens, temples and seasonal exhibitions. Growers train them into elaborate displays, from single giant flowers to sculpted cascades.
plants.bloomingSeason: September through November, with late varieties peaking in autumn
plants.location: Japan, in gardens, shrines and autumn chrysanthemum shows
plants.funFact: The chrysanthemum is Japan's imperial flower. Its sixteen-petal design appears on the emperor's seal and on the country's passports.
